_about: Household-facing summary of the Benchmarks tab of Gregor Posadas's PH Water Service Obligations Inventory (preliminary, Nov 2026). Status: binding = binding, official text read; unconfirmed = binding but not yet confirmed from official text; target = national target or design guide, not binding; none = no binding rule found.

wd.name: Water district
wd.plain: A local government-owned water utility, created under PD 198 and overseen by LWUA.

mwss.name: Metro Manila concessionaire
mwss.plain: Manila Water or Maynilad, private companies running MWSS's system under a concession agreement.

private.name: Private utility (NWRB-regulated)
private.plain: A private water company holding a Certificate of Public Convenience from the National Water Resources Board.

lgu.name: LGU-run utility
lgu.plain: A water system run directly by the city or municipal government.

community.name: Community system
community.plain: A barangay waterworks association, rural waterworks association or cooperative.

dimensions.title: Hours of water each day
dimensions.question: How many hours a day you should have water at the tap

wd.text: No minimum. LWUA and the state auditor track the share of homes with 24/7 water, but each district sets its own target. If a private partner runs your district, its contract may promise 24 hours.
wd.cite: LWUA-DBM JMC 2023-1, Form A, indicator 2; LWUA MC 011-18

lgu.text: At least 18 hours a day (12 hours if classed as Category B under NWRB's 2018 rules).
lgu.cite: NWRB Res. 14-0921, via JMC 02 s.2024, p. 7

community.text: No minimum. NWRB's 2018 rules set no numbers for community-based systems.

target.cite: Philippine Water Supply and Sanitation Master Plan 2019-2030, p. 37

dimensions.title: Water pressure
dimensions.question: How strong the flow at your connection should be

wd.text: No minimum. LWUA's performance indicators don't measure pressure at all. Some private-partner contracts promise 10 psi.

mwss.text: At least 7 psi (about 5 meters of head) at the connection.

lgu.cite: NWRB Res. 14-0921, via JMC 02 s.2024, p. 7

target.text: National target: at least 7 meters (about 10 psi) at piped household connections.

dimensions.title: Safe, clean water
dimensions.question: What your drinking water must meet

_all.text: Philippine National Standards for Drinking Water 2017: no E. coli or coliform, turbidity under 5 NTU, chlorine residual 0.3-1.5 mg/L, arsenic and lead under 0.01 mg/L, and limits on color, taste and odor.

wd.text: After 15 or more days without water, the district may not disconnect you or charge the minimum charge. Repair times are set in each district's Citizen's Charter.

mwss.text: At least 48 hours' notice before planned interruptions; unplanned ones restored within 6 hours. Bill rebates when failures last over 15 days.

private.text: No rule on notice or restoration times found.

lgu.text: No rule on notice or restoration times found.

community.text: No rule on notice or restoration times found.

dimensions.title: Response to complaints
dimensions.question: How fast someone must act on your complaint

wd.text: The district must follow its Citizen's Charter complaint procedure. Complaints sent through the 8888 hotline must be acted on within 72 hours.

mwss.text: The concessionaire's consumer desk must act "with dispatch" (no time limit set).

private.text: Complaints filed with the NWRB Board: answer within 10 days, decision within 60 days.

lgu.text: Citizen's Charter procedure; 8888 complaints acted on within 72 hours.

community.text: Complaints can go to NWRB if the system is registered there.

dimensions.title: Your water bill
dimensions.question: Rules on what you can be charged

wd.text: Rates are reviewed by LWUA. A public hearing is required before every increase, and each increase can be at most 60% of the current rate.

mwss.text: "Fair and reasonable" rates set by the MWSS Regulatory Office.

private.text: Rates follow NWRB's tariff method; return on investment capped at 12%.

lgu.text: Rates are set by the local council.

community.text: Rates are self-set; no outside review found.

dimensions.title: Getting connected
dimensions.question: How long a new connection application can take

wd.text: 3, 7 or 20 working days for simple, complex or highly technical applications, with written reasons if denied.

mwss.text: RA 11032 processing times do not bind private operators.

private.text: RA 11032 processing times do not bind private operators.

lgu.text: 3, 7 or 20 working days for simple, complex or highly technical applications.

_all.text: Bacteriological tests at least every 6 months and chemical tests every 12 months, at DOH-accredited labs.
A sanitary survey within 24 hours of a positive E. coli result, and a boil-water advisory if it persists.
An approved Water Safety Plan covering source to tap.

wd.text: No duty to publish water-quality results; they go to the local health office only. Joint-venture agreements must be posted within 5 working days.
wd.cite: DOH AO 2017-0010, p. 6; NEDA JV Guidelines 2023, p. 11

mwss.text: Annual report to Congress on coverage.

lgu.text: The LGU monitoring committee must "inform the public" about local water quality (no frequency set).

wd.text: The district holds an exclusive franchise but has no legal duty to extend service across its area.

lgu.text: LGUs must "provide" water systems, with no service level.

jv.text: Joint venture contracts reviewed (BACIWA, San Jose) promise 24-hour supply within 2 to 5 years and 10 psi within 4 to 5 years. Only the water district's board can enforce them, by forfeiting the operator's performance bond or ending the contract. The contract's targets are usually not public, but some districts publish an annual JV compliance report.
jv.cite: BACIWA-PrimeWater JVA Secs. 5.1.2, 5.3; San Jose WD JV Implementation Report 2023
